subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Aisha —

Great to meet you and Samir earlier. Thanks for walking us through FinBot’s transaction summarization pipeline — below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap / pain points we heard
- Unit economics are the biggest blocker: inference spend has grown 3x in the last 6 months as usage ramped.
- Current stack: self-hosted Llama2-like variant on GCP (n1/p4-like), mostly single-request calls (no batching), no KV/prefix caching.
- Quality sensitivity: you need parity for key downstream signals (fraud flags, summary correctness).
- Latency SLO: 95% under 450ms currently; target is improving p50 to <200ms for UX features.

Success criteria you shared
- Reduce inference cost per 1k tokens by ~40-60% without degrading QA metrics (summary accuracy, false positives).
- Keep 95p latency within acceptable bound for critical flows.
- Controlled rollout to a subset of traffic and easy rollback.

What Redwood can help with (high level)
- Cost levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, model variant recommendations & quantization, better kernel selection to reduce GPU time.
- PoC plan: run a small workload on a dedicated Redwood PoC cluster using representative traffic to measure unit economics and QA metrics.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a week-of-traffic histogram and a representative sample (anonymized) of requests? (I attached a template CSV).
2) Permission to run a 2-week PoC on ~5-10% of traffic or on a captured workload.
3) Quick follow-up: propose Wed 4/14 at 10am PT for a technical sync with Rishi (our inference lead) — OK?

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (pricing scenarios), poc-plan-draft.pdf (high-level PoC), finbot-usage-histogram.csv (template)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi on the technical approach once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samir Nair <samir.nair@finbot.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Infrastructure: we self-host on GCP using a mix of n1-standard + p4-equivalent GPUs for model serving. We previously tried batching but reverted because of memory pressure and complexity.
- Volume: ~1.8B tokens / month across summarization and classification flows; peak QPS ~1200 (short bursts during market opens).
- Quality: we can tolerate small bumps in per-token LM accuracy for non-critical flows but not for fraud-detection summaries.
- Quantization openness: we’re cautious — open to 8-bit or 4-bit if you can demonstrate negligible quality regression on our evals.

We’ll attach the usage histogram and a small anonymized sample by EOD Tue.

PoC: we’re supportive of a PoC. Please send a short statement of work (duration, success metrics, expected cost to us for the PoC if any).

One ask: can you give a rough ballpark on achievable unit-cost reduction (percent) if we enable batching + KV caching + 8-bit quantization? Even a range will help our procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to Wed.

—Aisha
Aisha Shah
Head of ML Platform, FinBot
aisha.shah@finbot.ai

--
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Aisha —

Appreciate the details. That volume and peak pattern is helpful.

Quick answers:
- Ballpark: with batching (~2-4x tokens-per-GPU request where latency tail allows), KV/prefix caching for repeat context, and 8-bit quantization we typically see 35-65% reduction in token unit-cost depending on latency targets and model family. If you push aggressive batching and are OK with slightly higher tail for non-critical flows, the high end is achievable.
- PoC SOW: attaching a one-page PoC plan (poc-plan-draft.pdf). Proposed 2 weeks: week 1 validation & baseline collection, week 2 optimization runs and metric comparison. Success metrics: >=40% cost reduction for non-critical traffic; no >2% degradation in summary accuracy for critical flows; latency p95 within agreed bound.

Ben, looping you and Rishi to coordinate the PoC cluster sizing and to propose a minimal dataset for quality checks.

Aisha — can you confirm the Wed 4/14 10am PT time?

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Aisha / Marissa —

Thanks for the context, Aisha. Quick technical notes ahead of Wed:
- Baseline measurements we’ll need: per-endpoint tokens/request, latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99), and a few hundred representative request samples (anonymized). The finbot-usage-histogram.csv template Marissa attached will work.
- PoC plan (high level):
  * Week 1: ingest captured workload, run baseline on a small Redwood PoC cluster using your current model variant to reproduce current costs.
  * Week 2: iterate with batching (gradually increase batch sizes), enable KV caching for any repeat prefixes, then evaluate 8-bit quantization on a copy of the weights with our quality regression harness.
- Expected impact: conservative estimate 35-45% cost reduction with safe latency constraints; aggressive tuning (batched non-critical paths + caching + quantization) could push to 55-65% for those non-critical flows. Critical flows we’ll optimize for <5% quality delta first.

Deliverables: baseline report (cost/latency/quality), optimization run results, configuration recipes (batch sizes, cache TTLs), and a roll-forward plan for production.

Action items for Aisha / FinBot before Wed:
- Share the anonymized sample + histogram (Aisha said EOD Tue).
- Confirm which endpoints are non-critical vs critical.

We’ll have an internal checklist for the PoC cluster sizing. Marissa — I attached a short PoC checklist PDF.

See you Wed 10am PT.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
